section_summary.extract_value: This limitations and future directions section notes the study used a cross-sectional sample of Black older adolescent females admitted to public universities in the southeastern U.S., limiting generalizability (e.g., not representative of Black males or females in other regions) and precluding causal inference. It also highlights measurement issues (negatively-worded items for body image flexibility requiring reverse-scoring), potential biases from missing data, and recommends future experimental and psychometric work and inclusion of culturally-relevant appearance dimensions.
section_summary.evidence_source: Selected sentences: 'Our sample exclusively consisted of Black older adolescent females who primarily resided in and were admitted to public universities in the southeastern U.S.'; 'Thus, our findings are neither representative of the prospective first-year Black male experience nor likely of their female counterparts living in other regions of the country.'; 'Moreover, our cross-sectional design precludes any causal inferences.'; 'Also, we contend that body image flexibility merits consideration as a component of positive body image. Yet, from a psychometric and conceptual standpoint, all items were negatively-worded and thus needed to be reverse-scored.'
